what_office_does.text: The lieutenant governor takes over the governor’s duties when the governor is absent from the state or leaves office, and presides over the State Senate with a tie-breaking vote. The office also chairs the Commission for Economic Development and serves on the State Lands Commission, Ocean Protection Council, and boards of California’s university systems.
what_office_does.label: fact

candidates.name: Fiona Ma

says.text: Ma wants a more affordable California and less government red tape that delays housing and discourages business investment.
says.label: value

says.text: Ma names accountability, transparency, fixing broken systems, and cutting waste as priorities in public office.
says.label: value

says.text: Ma proposes making higher education more affordable, expanding paid internships, and strengthening pathways to careers.
says.label: value
says.quote: As Lieutenant Governor, I will make higher education more affordable, expand paid internships, and strengthen career pathways.

candidates.core_case: Ma presents her financial training and public-service experience as tools for making California more affordable while supporting economic growth. She emphasizes working with communities across all 58 counties and connecting affordable education to career opportunities.

candidates.name: Gloria Romero

says.text: Romero proposes restoring education standards, defending Title IX for girls in sports, and fighting antisemitism on college campuses.
says.label: value

says.text: Romero wants an economic plan that helps businesses thrive and criticizes bureaucracy and waste in California’s budget.
says.label: value

says.text: Romero proposes reining in commissions she describes as politicized, with a focus on protecting water, farmland, and Californians’ way of life.
says.label: value

candidates.core_case: Romero presents her legislative experience and break with one-party rule as a basis for challenging Sacramento’s existing approach. She proposes using the office actively to raise education standards, support businesses, and change how state commissions operate.

where_they_differ.text: Both emphasize affordability and government reform, but Ma focuses on financial management, affordable higher education, and career opportunities. Romero focuses on challenging one-party rule, restoring school standards, changing state commissions, and addressing Title IX and campus antisemitism.
